title: Tail Expressions
concept: The last expression in a block (without a semicolon) becomes the value of that block — an implicit return.
why: Tail expressions let you write concise functions without explicit `return` — the last line IS the return value.
tips: No semicolon on the last line = it becomes the return value
Semicolon on the last line = value discarded, returns Unit
Tail expressions work in any block, not just functions
Tail expressions make simple functions more readable and concise
common_mistakes: Accidentally putting a semicolon on the tail expression — returns Unit instead!
Using both `return` AND a tail expression — `return` wins
Forgetting that the tail expression must match the declared return type
